findings.title: Shared module-level SSLContext is mutated by per-request client certs
findings.suggested_fix: Only inject the preloaded context when no client cert is given: `elif verify is True and client_cert is None: pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context`. For verify=True with a client cert, either set pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] to the default bundle path (old behavior) or build a fresh context per pool (create_urllib3_context + load_verify_locations). Assumption: correctness of the client-cert path matters more than the load-time savings for that uncommon case.

residual_risks: The module-level context is built at import time from DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH; a missing or unreadable certifi bundle now raises when requests is imported, not when a verify=True request is made. Environments that only use verify=False or custom bundles would fail earlier than before.
Not verified: behavior with urllib3 1.26.x, where pool_kwargs ssl_context handling and the load_cert_chain-on-supplied-context path may differ (pyproject allows urllib3<3).
testing_gaps: No test covers verify=True combined with cert=(cert, key) to assert the shared _preloaded_ssl_context is not mutated or reused across differing client certs.

findings.title: Shared module-level SSLContext accumulates client certs across hosts and sessions (CWE-284/CWE-200)
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, only set pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] = _preloaded_ssl_context when verify is True AND client_cert is None. When a client cert is supplied, fall back to per-connection contexts (e.g. pool_kwargs['ca_certs'] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)) so load_cert_chain never touches the shared context. Assumes losing the perf optimisation for mTLS requests is acceptable.

findings.title: verify=True silently overrides user-configured ssl_context in HTTPAdapter subclasses (CWE-327/CWE-295)
findings.suggested_fix: In HTTPAdapter._get_connection (or _urllib3_request_context), skip injecting _preloaded_ssl_context when self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw already contains an 'ssl_context'. Otherwise fall back to the previous behaviour (ca_certs on the connection) so the user's context is honored.

residual_risks: The shared context is also mutated by urllib3 per connection (verify_mode set each time; check_hostname forced False when a subclass passes assert_hostname/assert_fingerprint via init_poolmanager), so those settings could persist onto later unrelated connections. I did not reproduce this.
Concurrent load_cert_chain / verify_mode writes on one SSLContext from multiple threads were not examined for thread-safety.
testing_gaps: No test covers cert=(cert,key) followed by a cert-less verify=True request to confirm the client cert is not carried over via the shared context.
No test covers an HTTPAdapter subclass that supplies its own ssl_context via init_poolmanager under verify=True.

findings.title: Shared module-level SSLContext leaks client certs across sessions and threads
findings.suggested_fix: Use the shared preloaded context only when client_cert is None (add `and client_cert is None`, or set ssl_context only in that case). When a client cert is supplied, fall back to per-connection contexts (leave ssl_context unset and set ca_certs to the default bundle) or copy the preloaded context per pool key. Assumption: mTLS callers accept the per-connection load_verify_locations cost.

findings.title: Per-request ssl_context overrides custom ssl_context from HTTPAdapter.init_poolmanager subclasses
findings.suggested_fix: Have _urllib3_request_context/_get_connection skip injecting the default context when the adapter's poolmanager.connection_pool_kw already has an ssl_context (make the helper aware of the adapter's pool kwargs, or drop the default from pool_kwargs when 'ssl_context' is already set on the manager). Assumption: an explicit user context should always win over the shared default.

findings.title: Eager import-time CA load makes 'import requests' fail when the bundle is missing
findings.suggested_fix: Build the preloaded context lazily on first verify=True use (functools.lru_cache or a guarded module-level getter called from _urllib3_request_context). Raise the existing OSError('Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle...') if the bundle is missing. This keeps the one-time load cost and restores import safety.

residual_risks: Code that calls HTTPAdapter.cert_verify(conn, url, True, cert) on a pool obtained outside _get_connection (legacy get_connection()-then-cert_verify subclasses overriding send) no longer gets ca_certs set. urllib3 then falls back to the OS trust store via load_default_certs() rather than certifi, silently changing the trust anchors. Not verified against a concrete third-party adapter.
The bundle is snapshotted at import, so a long-lived process never sees an updated or rotated certifi bundle file until restart. This is likely acceptable for the stated performance goal.
testing_gaps: No test covers client-cert (mTLS) requests followed by a cert-less verify=True request in the same process, which would expose the shared-context cert leak. The existing mTLS test only uses verify=False.
No test covers an HTTPAdapter subclass passing ssl_context via init_poolmanager combined with verify=True.

findings.title: Shared module-level SSLContext gets client cert loaded; no test covers verify=True with cert
findings.suggested_fix: Do not hand the shared context to urllib3 when client_cert is not None (fall back to ca_certs=DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH-style loading, or copy the context per pool). Add a regression test: send an mTLS request with verify=True and cert=..., then a second verify=True request without cert to a server that records getpeercert(), and assert no client cert is presented. Also add a unit test on _urllib3_request_context(verify=True, client_cert=...) asserting the resulting ssl_context is not the shared module object.

findings.title: Adapter-level custom ssl_context silently overridden for verify=True; untested
findings.suggested_fix: Only inject _preloaded_ssl_context when the adapter has not configured one, for example by checking self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw.get('ssl_context') in _get_connection before calling connection_from_host. Add a test that mounts an adapter subclass whose init_poolmanager supplies ssl_context and asserts that context reaches the connection for verify=True.

findings.title: New ca_cert_dir branch and verify=True positive path have no tests
findings.suggested_fix: Add unit tests calling _urllib3_request_context directly: verify=True gives ssl_context is requests.adapters._preloaded_ssl_context and no ca_certs; verify=<tmp dir> gives ca_cert_dir; verify=<file> gives ca_certs; verify=False gives CERT_NONE with no ssl_context. Add a cert_verify test asserting conn.ca_certs / ca_cert_dir stay untouched for verify=True and are set for a str path (file and dir).

residual_risks: Import-time behavior change: the missing-default-bundle OSError ('Could not find a suitable TLS CA certificate bundle') used to be raised per request for verify=True; it is now raised (as a different error) when requests.adapters is imported, and no test covers the missing-bundle case.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that verify=True requests avoid per-connection load_verify_locations (e.g. conn.ca_certs stays None after cert_verify), so the performance intent has no regression guard.
verify=True combined with a proxy (proxy_manager_for + pool_kwargs ssl_context) is untested.
